alt: Five modes: written (headlines, captions), spoken (voice, tone, pace), visual (photos, colour, icons), spatial (layout, position, size, white space) and aural (music, sound effects, silence). A text is multimodal when it combines two or more. Criteria A and B both include visual and spatial aspects.
caption: Visuals and layout are part of the meaning, not decoration.

alt: Nine elements to check: subject, foreground and background, shot distance, angle, gaze, colour, typography, layout and symbols, each with a question. Then state the denotation, what is literally there (a green headline), before the connotation, what it suggests (nature, recycling or “go”), which depends on culture.
caption: Describe precisely first; connotation without a named detail is just opinion.

after: ## 3. How words and images work together
alt: Four relationships: anchor, where words fix an open image’s meaning (an empty beach reads as peace or loss depending on the caption); reinforce, where both say the same thing; extend, where one mode adds information the other lacks; and contrast, where they pull against each other for humour, irony or shock.
caption: Name the relationship before you explain its effect.

alt: A schematic leaflet: a lone runner on a rainy road photographed from a low angle, the headline “YOU ARE NOT RUNNING ALONE.” in thin white capitals, and forty orange runner icons with “Join 40 neighbours this Sunday.” The analysis describes it, names the relationships (the headline contrasts with the photo; the icons extend it), interprets the move from loneliness to a group, and identifies values of community and support.
caption: Describe, name the relationship, interpret, then identify values and attitudes.

after: ## 4. Sound and image in spoken multimodal texts
alt: A timeline of a library video in rows for what is heard, seen and played. A calm voice says “Our library is quiet” while teenagers laugh around a game table; upbeat music starts on “but”: “But it’s never boring.” The image contrasts with the words and the music marks the turn, aiming the video at young people who think libraries are dull.
caption: Pair what you heard with what was on screen at the same moment.

after: ## 5. From description to interpretation: a method
alt: A three-step method: notice one specific detail, connect it to the words or sound, and explain its effect and the values behind it. Below, model sentences at each level: emergent describes with one simple reason; capable links the visual to the words and the purpose; proficient interprets implicit attitudes and compares modes.
caption: The method is the same at every level; the depth of explanation grows.
